answer:
Keep them as two specimens, document the relationship, and preserve both 1968 accession numbers. A single identity is available to you only as a *third*, newly declared entity that both segments are parts of — never as a merger that dissolves the two. Here is why, and what to write down.

**1. What each accessioned segment is.** Model each boxed core segment twice over, which CRMsci explicitly sanctions: as an S13 Sample and as an E19 Physical Object. S1 Matter Removal's scope note says the removed matter may acquire a persistent identity of a different nature beyond the act of its removal, such as becoming a physical object in the narrower sense, and that such cases should be modelled by multiple instantiation. You need both aspects, and the tool output makes the reason concrete: S13's applicable-property list carries neither P30 transferred custody of, nor P46 is composed of, nor any keeper or location property, so a bare S13 cannot hold a loan history or a part-whole assertion. The E19 aspect carries custody, location, parts and the accession identifier; the S13 aspect carries what makes the thing a *sample* — S13's scope note names "the layering of a bore core" as the representative quality whose corruption ends the sample's existence.

**2. Why not one specimen.** Identity here is not a free administrative choice at the level of the matter. S11 Amount of Matter, S13's parent, states that what matters for the identity of an amount of matter is the preservation of a relevant composition from its initial state of definition onwards, and names "the sequence of layers of a bore core" as exactly such a criterion. Each segment has its own initial state of definition: its own S2 Sample Taking, six weeks apart, at its own O4 sampled at spot forty metres away, logged and numbered by its own crew. Two definitions, two samples. Martin Doerr put the underlying principle to the SIG when this scope note was being drafted: "There is no natural identity to something material" — you have to say under which category you are considering the matter, and the category has to supply identity criteria in advance, for a purpose. For a core segment the category is "sample", and its criterion is the layer sequence it was taken to witness; that criterion attaches to each coring separately.

On the object side, the only things that could turn two physical things into one are events: E81 Transformation, which would take both segments out of existence, or E79 Part Addition, which requires that someone actually join them (P110 augmented, P111 added). Neither has happened — the boxes have sat in two buildings for fifty years. A stratigrapher re-reading old logs in the present is not an event acting on the rock; it is an assertion about it.

**A tension in the premise worth stating plainly.** Two boreholes forty metres apart cannot yield two core segments that are one continuous piece of rock: each hole removes its own column, and the bottom of one column and the top of the other are forty metres apart laterally. What can be continuous — and what "struck the same fault zone" actually means — is the geological body both holes intersected, plus a depth correlation between the two logs. CRM forces those two kinds of continuity into different places, which is precisely why it is worth separating them. The recommendation below is the same either way, but the relationship you record differs.

**3. Where the continuity goes.**

(a) *The shared source body.* Model the fault zone / correlated interval in the ground as a stratigraphic unit: A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit in CRMarchaeo (A2 subclass of A8 Stratigraphic Unit, subclass of S20 Rigid Physical Feature, subclass of E26 Physical Feature). Then hang both corings off that one body: each S2 Sample Taking O3 sampled from it, O4 sampled at its own borehole spot, O5 removed its own S13 Sample. That records "same fault zone, two holes, two spots" exactly, and keeps the forty metres visible instead of hiding it inside a merged specimen. If the fault surface itself needs relating to the volumes it cuts, AP11 has physical relation to (typed through AP11.1 has type) is built for it; its scope note explicitly covers earthquake-induced faults and speaks of archaeological *or geological* documentation.

(b) *The claim itself.* The stratigrapher's correlation is an inference drawn from old records, not an observation of the cores, so record it as an S6 Data Evaluation — the CRMsci class for concluding propositions about reality from observational data — P14 carried out by the stratigrapher, P4 has time-span now, J2 concluded that an I2 Belief, and J5 holds to be a belief value. That keeps the correlation attributable, dated and defeasible, which is the whole point: it reverses a 1968 reading and may itself be revised.

(c) *Only if you want a single handle for the correlated whole:* declare a further E19 Physical Object, the reconstructed interval, and assert P46 forms part of from each segment to it (at sample level the corresponding statement is O25 contains, of which P46 is a subproperty). This is additive — both segments keep their identity, their identifiers and their loan histories. Note that CRM has no property meaning "is physically continuous with": connect E18 E18 offers only P46 is composed of, P130 shows features of and P198 holds or supports. Declaring a whole is therefore the only way to say it, and a declared whole is exactly what does *not* require erasing the parts.

**4. The old loan records, and what you must honour.** The two accession numbers must keep pointing at the same two things they pointed at in 1968. The model is what makes that true, not politeness:

- Each number stays an E42 Identifier linked by P1 is identified by to its own segment. P1 is a shortcut for the identifier-assignment path (connect E15 E42 prints the full path through P140i was attributed by and P37 assigned), so the fully explicit form is to keep the two original E15 Identifier Assignment events, each with its crew as P14 carried out by and its 1968 P4 has time-span.
- Each loan is an E10 Transfer of Custody, and the CRM quantifies P30 transferred custody of as *necessary* on E10. Collapse the two segments into one specimen and every historical loan silently changes its referent; worse, each repository becomes the keeper of no more than a part of one specimen. E10's scope note demands that where custody is of a representative part, the way that part is defined make it unambiguous who keeps a part and who the whole, and be consistent with the identity criteria of the kept thing. Two buildings each holding half of a single specimen is precisely the ambiguity it warns against. The same scope note also records that CRM models legal ownership and physical custody separately and leaves institutions to compose their own notion of "accession" from them — so an accession number is a curatorial handle, not a decree about physical identity.
- If the survey nevertheless wants to work under one number from now on, add it rather than rewrite: a new E15 Identifier Assignment, P37 assigned the new E42, P14 carried out by, P4 has time-span, and P48 has preferred identifier on the *new whole*, not on either segment. Deassignment is available and is not forbidden — SIG Issue 630, closed as Done at the 57th meeting (Marseille, October 2023), redrafted P38 deassigned so that it means the actor carrying out the assignment "has decided no more to use the respective identifier", listing among the reasons the case where "items are merged or split up in a collection". But note what that makes de-assignment: a dated act by a named actor, scoped to items in its possession, and prospective. It says the survey no longer uses the code; it does not say the code never identified the segment. That is why it leaves the loan paperwork true. What you must not do is delete an identifier or repoint it at a different thing — and per Modelling principles > Monotonicity the 1968 assertions were correct when made and stay in the record.

**Bottom line:** two specimens (each an S13 Sample and an E19 Physical Object), one shared stratigraphic body they were both sampled from, one dated and attributed correlation belief, both accession numbers preserved and both loan histories intact. If a single identity is wanted for the correlated interval, mint it as a new whole with P46 parts, and give it its own new number.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: This is what merging the two into one specimen would actually require: P124 transformed the two segments, P123 resulted in a single new thing, with the inputs simultaneously taken out of existence. No physical event has occurred — nobody touched the rock — and an E81 would destroy the very entities the 1968 loan records transferred custody of.

The legitimate route to one physical whole, but only if someone physically joins the segments (P110 augmented, P111 added). They are boxed in two different repository buildings. If they were ever brought together and joined, this is the class to use, and it would still create a whole with the two as parts rather than abolish the parts.

rejected_alternatives.option: S24 Sample Splitting (with O27 split, O29 removed sub-sample)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: CRMsci's machinery for one sample becoming several. It is the mirror image of this case and does not apply: these were two independent instances of S2 Sample Taking, not one sample divided. Martin Doerr raised exactly the bore-core version of the split case to the SIG — "If we have a bore core, we can split it along the drilling direction" — which is the situation this case is not.

rejected_alternatives.option: E91 Co-Reference Assignment / L54 is same as
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Where the claim would live if you believed the two catalogue records denote one real thing. But E91 was withdrawn from the CRM text (Issue 230, Done, closed February 2015, and referred to CRMinf), CRMdig's L54 is defined only as a non-unique identification, and more decisively the two segments are not co-referent: they are two distinct amounts of matter removed by two distinct events.

Tempting as a way to bracket the two boxes together, but its scope note is about aggregations assembled and maintained to a collection development plan, and it explicitly directs that things forming wholes — physically bound, or kept together for their functionality — be documented as E19 Physical Object instead. It says nothing about physical continuity, and the two segments are curated by two different buildings, not as one holding.

rejected_alternatives.option: Deleting or repointing one of the 1968 accession numbers
rejected_alternatives.why_not: The move the case is really asking about, and the one to refuse. It falsifies fifty years of loan paperwork and breaks Monotonicity. If consolidation is genuinely wanted, the sanctioned form is a new E15 Identifier Assignment that P37 assigns a new identifier and, if the survey insists, P38 deassigns an old one — prospective and attributed, leaving the historical record standing.

siblings_considered.why_not: S12 Amount of Fluid is S13's only sibling under S11 Amount of Matter. A boxed rock core is not a confined quantity of fluid, and nothing in this case turns on fluid confinement; what the segments are is matter taken to be representative of a formation, which is S13.

While still in the ground the interval was a physical feature — and I do use a feature class (via A2) for the fault zone itself. But an E26 cannot be separated from its carrier object and has no natural boundaries; the boxed segments have objective boundaries, have been moved between buildings and have been loaned out. Once cored, they are E19 Physical Objects, i.e. units for documentation.

E80 Part Removal is the other subclass of S1 Matter Removal. It would frame the segments as pieces detached from an already documented whole, which is the very implication the stratigrapher's claim must not be allowed to smuggle in. The 1968 corings took matter as a representative witness of a geological formation, which is what S2 Sample Taking is for, and each coring produced its own sample.

A3 Stratigraphic Interface is the surface between units. The fault zone as intersected at depth is a body of rock, so A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit is right. If the fault plane itself needs modelling, A3 is the class, and AP11 has physical relation to is what relates it to the volumes it cuts — its scope note names earthquake-induced faults for that purpose.

S8 Categorical Hypothesis Building covers law-like assumptions induced from many observations. The stratigrapher's correlation is a particular claim about two particular cores, concluded from existing log data, which is what S6 Data Evaluation is defined for. (S7 Simulation or Prediction, the other sibling, is out: no model is being executed.)

E3 Condition State is the other subclass of E2 Temporal Entity a curator would reach for, and it records the physical state of preservation of the segments over a period. The correlation is not a state of the rock; it is a proposition an actor holds to be true, which is I2 Belief, with a belief value via J5.

E35 Title covers strings recognisable as titles within a cultural context. Accession numbers are organisational codes intended to identify uniquely and permanently within one or more organisations, which is E42 Identifier — and only E42 is the range of P37, P38 and P48, the properties this case needs.

E17 Type Assignment would record classifying the segments — as fault breccia, say, or as correlative. The act at issue is allocating or retiring an inventory code and recording who did so and when, and only E15 Identifier Assignment carries P37 assigned and P38 deassigned.

E8 Acquisition transfers legal ownership. The loan paperwork moved physical custody only; the survey retained title throughout. E10's own scope note stresses that CRM models legal ownership and physical custody separately, and that institutions build their notion of accession from combinations of the two.

notes: Four friction points in the tools. (1) `concept S24` answers "No such concept" even though O27 split and O29 removed sub-sample both declare S24 Sample Splitting as their domain and S2's dossier lists S24 as a subclass; the sample-splitting class is reachable only through its properties, which made it hard to check whether the split machinery could be run in reverse. (2) `connect S2 A2` does not offer O3 sampled from, although A2 is an S10 Material Substantial by declaration (A2 < A8 < S20 < E26 < E18, and CRMsci declares S10 as superclass of E18). The traversal appears not to cross from CRMbase upward into the CRMsci abstraction, so I had to assemble that path by hand from the individual dossiers — worth double-checking before implementing. (3) `quote` refuses a class identifier as a source ("not a thread, episode, message or document chunk id"), so the scope-note wording I lean on most — E10 on representative parts and identity criteria, E19 on documentation units, S11 on identity from the initial state of definition — could not be quote-verified. I paraphrased it rather than putting it in quotation marks; it is all visible in the `concept` output for those classes. (4) `thread t1123`, which the episode index labels "Modeling finds as objects versus stratigraphic units in CRMarcheo" (a precedent that would have supported keeping the specimen distinct from the stratigraphic unit), printed a thread beginning with an unrelated 2018-09-01 message on E41 versus rdfs:label, so I could not confirm that precedent and left it out of the answer. Substantively, the one thing I could not settle from the corpus is the case's own factual premise: two holes forty metres apart cannot produce physically continuous core, so I answered for both readings and said so rather than picking one silently.
